articles.title: “You have to make an effort”: Travis Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce opens up about her life as she supports Jason Kelce’s children
articles.summary: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, and his older brother, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ icon, Jason Kelce, have built a life of luxury
articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, and his older brother, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ icon, Jason Kelce, have built a life of luxury through their own hard work. While the two remain popular faces, they have also often expressed gratitude to their mother, Donna Kelce. Amid the new season, Donna Kelce has reflected on an important aspect of her life.Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce weighs in on being a supportive grandparentIn an interview with PEOPLE, Travis Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce said, "I've been very fortunate because I worked most of my life to be able to travel. That's the one thing I try as much as I can without being a pest. I try to show up…”The Kansas City Chiefs’ star player’s mother added, “I know a lot of grandparents get upset and say, 'Well, why don't you come to my house?' You can't do that. You're disrupting them." "Grandparents need to travel to their children. That's just the way it is. Otherwise, you become a burden. That's the way I feel," she adds. "So if you want to see your kids, go visit them. Quit telling them, 'Why don't you come to my house?' No, go visit."Donna Kelce continued, "I think it's important to just show up and let them know that you care as much as you can," she says. "It's difficult with everybody's busy lives, but you have to make an effort if you can. I mean, some people can't. They can't afford that. I'm fortunate enough to be able to do that, so it's good."Donna Kelce also reflected on Travis Kelce being an uncle as she said, "It's kind of like a free-for-all where he's throwing them up in the air and on the couch," she said. "Jason does the same thing. It's just amazing to see your grown-up children interact with their own kids. It's very heartwarming."Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce have often credited their mother, Donna Kelce, for all the success they have achievedDespite being one of the most popular faces in the country, owing to both her sons’ success on the field, Donna Kelce has adjusted well to her newfound fame.Donna Kelce has been extremely supportive of both her sons and has been there for them through all the challenges they faced in their professional and personal lives.While there has been a considerable amount of buzz around Travis Kelce’s marriage life, Donna Kelce has helped him maintain complete privacy over it as she has often helped him to dismiss any negative rumors about his personal life.For now, all eyes remain on Travis Kelce as he gears up for the Week 5 clash.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Guy Loves Ball": Ex-Bears pro bowler backs Mike Evans’ 150% tax hike gamble to chase another Super Bowl ring
articles.summary: Mike Evans has given up a more lucrative offer to join the San Francisco 49ers, and former Chicago Bears Pro Bowler Kyle Long believes the decision says
articles.body: Mike Evans has given up a more lucrative offer to join the San Francisco 49ers, and former Chicago Bears Pro Bowler Kyle Long believes the decision says plenty about the veteran receiver’s priorities. Long praised Evans after San Francisco beat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29, highlighting the financial sacrifice involved in leaving Florida for California. Evans caught seven passes for 113 yards and a touchdown in the win, helping the 49ers improve to 5-0. At this stage of his career, Evans appears focused on another Super Bowl ring, even if the move costs him more in taxes.Kyle Long praises Mike Evans for choosing the 49ers over more moneyLong summed up his reaction in a post on X, writing, “Less money and about 150% hike on income tax … guy loves ball and #winning,”The comment reflects the financial difference Evans faces after leaving the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he spent 12 seasons. Florida has no state income tax, while California's top marginal income tax rate reached 13.3% in 2025. However, Long's 150% figure is an estimate, not a confirmed calculation of Evans' personal tax increase.The contract figures also make the decision interesting. Evans signed a three-year deal with San Francisco worth up to $60.4 million, including $16.3 million guaranteed. Tampa Bay was prepared to offer more, according to general manager Jason Licht.“We made a significantly higher offer [than the 49ers], and that was just the first offer,” Licht said in March.Evans did not hide the fact that money still matters to him. But when the 49ers introduced him, he explained why it was not the deciding factor.“I love money, obviously, like everybody else. But the money was not the biggest factor for me.”San Francisco gave Evans a fresh challenge and a chance to join a team he believed was close to winning another championship. Tight end George Kittle also played a role in recruiting him, helping convince the veteran receiver that the move was right.Mike Evans delivers as 49ers chase another Super BowlEvans' performance against Seattle offered an early example of why San Francisco wanted him. He caught seven of his 10 targets for 113 yards and a touchdown, giving quarterback Brock Purdy a reliable option in a tense divisional game.He also caught Purdy's two-point pass to put San Francisco ahead 29-26 in the fourth quarter. After Seattle tied the score, the 49ers secured the victory with a late 44-yard field goal from Eddy Piñeiro.The win matters beyond the standings. Evans arrived believing he could help complete an offense that needed another proven receiver.“I feel like they were one piece away, and I think that I’m that piece.”That confidence now has some early support. Evans missed much of the 2025 season through injury, playing just eight games and finishing with 368 receiving yards. His first strong showing against Seattle suggests he can still make a difference when the team needs him.San Francisco has started 5-0, and Evans has quickly become an important part of its attack. The season remains young, but his decision already looks less like a financial gamble and more like a calculated bet on a team he believes can win it all.For Long, the sacrifice speaks for itself. Evans could have earned more in Tampa Bay, yet he chose the opportunity he felt offered the better chance to compete for another championship.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Brittany Mahomes is helping the Kansas City Current turn a major sporting occasion into a statement of ambition. The women’s soccer club is preparing to welcome a record 18,000 supporters for its October 25 clash against the Washington Spirit, creating a milestone that extends beyond the pitch. With Patrick Mahomes also involved in the club’s ownership, the family’s investment in women’s soccer continues to attract attention. The upcoming event will combine football, entertainment and community spirit as the Current looks to strengthen its connection with fans during a crucial stage of the season.Brittany Mahomes promotes KC Current’s historic 18,000-fan attendance goalBrittany shared the club’s announcement on Instagram Stories on October 12, helping spread the word about its ambitious matchday plans. The Current wants to bring together 18,000 supporters for its “One Current 2026: Bigger Home. Bigger Future” event at CPKC Stadium and the nearby Current Landing.“The biggest matchday in club history,” the Current wrote on Instagram.The club also called on fans to support its postseason ambitions.“We need our 12th player for our playoff push on Oct. 25 at 4PM vs. Spirit as we look to set a new attendance record of 18,000.”The challenge is significant because CPKC Stadium, which opened in 2024, holds approximately 12,000 spectators. To reach the target, the club plans to welcome another 6,000 fans at Current Landing, where supporters can follow the game on a large outdoor screen.The event will begin at 1 p.m. local time, with kickoff scheduled for 4 p.m. Grounds Passes start at $10 and offer access to food trucks, games, giveaways and family-friendly activities.The first 10,000 attendees across both locations will receive an exclusive Kansas City Current flag. After the match, fans can stay for a Kansas City Chiefs watch party, connecting the two teams through a shared celebration of Kansas City sports.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany expand their KC Current investmentThe attendance push comes as the organization continues to build its facilities and media presence. The couple’s reported $325 million investment has drawn attention to the club’s growth, although the planned attendance record represents a separate achievement from the investment itself.Brittany also attended the August 3 opening of KC Current Studios, a facility designed for original shows, live broadcasts, podcasts and interviews. She brought her children, Sterling Skye and Patrick “Bronze” Lavon III, to the ceremony.In a video shared by the club, Brittany encouraged the children to speak into a microphone.“One, two, three,” Brittany said before Sterling and Bronze enthusiastically responded, “KC baby!”The Current celebrated the family moment with the caption, “@brittanylynne & the stars of the show at KC Current Studios,” while another post featuring the children was titled “Mahomes Mic Check.”Now, the club has another opportunity to turn its growing profile into a memorable fan experience. articles.title: Giants' Jameis Winston Likened to Michael Jordan, Abraham Lincoln by John Harbaugh in New Video
articles.summary: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston has spent the majority of his career as a backup, but his leadership ability is second to none.
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston has spent the majority of his career as a backup, but his leadership ability is second to none.

In fact, Giants head coach John Harbaugh went as far as to compare Winston to Abraham Lincoln and Michael Jordan.

"It's the best thing to be around, and it's genuine... He's a very strong Christian. He's a very good guy," Harbaugh told reporters Monday. "...He just doesn't let adversity get him down. It's like Michael Jordan or Abraham Lincoln. It's not how many times you get knocked down; it's how many times you get back up. You need to be plus-one in the 'get up' category."

Winston has faced his fair share of adversity throughout his career, from losing his starting job with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to bouncing from team to team, but he's managed to stay positive through it all.

His ability to stay positive is perhaps why he's forged such a successful career as a backup quarterback.

With starting quarterback Jaxson Dart out for the season, Winston will have the chance to prove himself under center. He had his best game of the season against the Washington Commanders on Sunday, throwing for 326 yards and three touchdowns in the tie.

He'll look to keep his momentum going into next week when he faces his former team, the New Orleans Saints.

articles.title: Chiefs billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt's $2 billion family background and the health battle that changed her dreams
articles.summary: Being born into one of America's wealthiest sports families opens many doors, but Gracie Hunt has built a public identity that reaches beyond her famous
articles.body: Being born into one of America's wealthiest sports families opens many doors, but Gracie Hunt has built a public identity that reaches beyond her famous surname. As the daughter of Kansas City Chiefs owner Clark Hunt and former Miss Kansas USA Tavia Hunt, she has grown up around football, fashion and philanthropy. Yet her journey has also included personal health struggles and a change in career dreams. From winning a beauty pageant to supporting charitable causes, Gracie has found ways to combine her interests with opportunities created by her family's legacy.Gracie Hunt balances the Chiefs, pageantry and a privileged upbringingGracelyn Hunt, widely known as Gracie, won the Miss Kansas USA title in 2021, following in her mother's footsteps. She graduated from Southern Methodist University with a degree in sports management and later pursued a master's degree at the University of Kansas.Her connection to the Chiefs extends beyond being the owner's daughter. She has worked in public relations for the franchise and regularly shares her enthusiasm for football with her social media followers. Growing up in a sports-focused household helped shape those interests, even though soccer was once her main ambition.The Hunt family has deep roots in American business. Gracie's great-grandfather, H. L. Hunt, founded Hunt Oil Company in 1936 and built a fortune through investments across several industries. Her father, Clark Hunt, chairs Hunt Sports Group and is a leading figure in the Chiefs organisation.The family has also enjoyed an affluent lifestyle in Highland Park, Dallas, where the reported family residence spans approximately 12,300 square feet. Gracie's own social media presence offers glimpses of designer fashion, travel and fitness, while her blog, Living Gracefully, reflects her wider interests.Gracie Hunt turns personal challenges into a purposeBehind the pageant titles and glamorous travel, Hunt has spoken openly about challenges that changed her plans. Soccer was her first love, and she once hoped to play at college level. However, four concussions forced her to reconsider that future.“Soccer was my first love,’ she explained to People magazine in November.’I wanted to play in college. I won the championship when I was in high school with my high school team and played club, as well.” She added, “After suffering four concussions that was a dream that I could no longer pursue, which is really hard when you work your entire life to be good at something. I had to find a new dream.’Hunt has also discussed living with celiac disease, which influenced her interest in nutrition and fitness. She explained, ‘I’ve known what it feels like to be really sick and to not know why. ER sick, on morphine sick, super sensitive to gluten and my parents couldn’t figure it out. The doctors couldn’t figure it out,’ she shared. ‘That really inspired me to become as educated as I could and get my nutrition accreditation.’Philanthropy has become another important part of her work. Hunt founded Breaking Barriers, a nonprofit focused on using sports to encourage inclusion and opportunity. She has also supported Special Olympics programmes, Make-A-Wish activities and youth sports initiatives.Explaining her motivation, she wrote, “Sports have broken barriers in my own life and given me a sense of identity and confidence. I grew up playing soccer and experienced firsthand how sports bring people together to work toward achieving a common goal. The power of sports diminishes the barriers formed by one’s unique walk of life—whether it be race, gender, belief, socioeconomic status, or language.”Her story combines privilege with personal setbacks, showing how she has used her platform to pursue interests beyond the football field.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tyreek Hill assault case takes new turn as responding officer challenges Keeta Vaccaro’s claims
articles.summary: The ongoing civil trial involving Miami Dolphins star Tyreek Hill and his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro Hill, has taken another important turn.
articles.body: The ongoing civil trial involving Miami Dolphins star Tyreek Hill and his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro Hill, has taken another important turn. A police officer who responded to a domestic disturbance call has offered testimony that could become significant as the court examines the allegations against the NFL wide receiver. Officer S. Cuellar described what Lakeeta told him during their initial interaction and clarified which claims she did not report at the time. His account has added another layer to the legal dispute, where both sides have presented sharply different versions of events.Tyreek Hill assault case: Officer S. Cuellar details his conversation with Lakeeta VaccaroAccording to Law&Crime Trials, Cuellar testified that Lakeeta told him arguments between the couple had become more frequent. She also reportedly described changes in Hill’s mood and said he could become aggressive.Lakeeta allegedly explained that she became concerned when Hill picked up their baby during an argument and began walking around the apartment before moving towards the balcony. She then contacted the police.However, Cuellar said he did not notice any scratches on Lakeeta’s legs when he arrived. During questioning, he confirmed that he would have arrested Hill if he had seen such injuries and Lakeeta had identified Hill as the person who caused them while tackling or wrestling with her.The officer also clarified that he did not recognise Hill when he first entered the apartment. He said his knowledge of the NFL star would not have influenced his professional judgment or his decision to document evidence of a possible crime.A key part of the testimony concerned what Lakeeta had reported during the encounter. Cuellar said she had not told him that Hill assaulted her, wrestled with her, threw her onto a desk or grabbed and injured her breasts. He added that he would have included those allegations in his report had she disclosed them.Lakeeta Vaccaro and Tyreek Hill offer conflicting accounts in courtCuellar’s testimony followed Lakeeta’s appearance in court on October 6. She described an alleged incident after the couple attended an event at ESPN headquarters. According to her testimony, Hill became angry when she declined professional hair and makeup services.Lakeeta alleged that Hill later tried to punch her stomach while she was pregnant because he did not want the baby. She said she blocked the attempted blow with her hands. She also described other alleged incidents involving pushing, pinching, hair-pulling and threats.Reflecting on her experience, Lakeeta testified, "I've been in this cycle with him for so long, being pregnant and realizing, what am I going to do? How am I going to get myself out of this,"Hill testified on October 7 and 8, denying that he physically abused, hit or assaulted his wife. He also accused her of taking $60,000 from him, arguing that they were not married when the alleged incident occurred.The couple married in November 2023 and welcomed their daughter, Capri, in November 2024. Lakeeta filed for divorce in April 2025 following a domestic disturbance call at their Florida home.The civil proceedings continue as the court considers testimony from both sides. articles.title: Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders reveal the small details that make a difference during demanding game days
articles.summary: Keeping makeup fresh through hours of heat, bright lights and energetic performances is no easy task.
articles.body: Keeping makeup fresh through hours of heat, bright lights and energetic performances is no easy task. Yet the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have mastered the art of maintaining a polished look long after the first application. Their game-day beauty routines offer useful lessons for anyone who struggles with melting foundation, fading blush or unwanted shine. From carefully layering products to using setting spray generously, these cheerleaders rely on practical techniques that help their makeup last. The best part? You do not need to perform on an NFL field to put these beauty secrets to work.Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders rely on primer, powder and setting sprayA long-lasting makeup routine starts well before the lipstick goes on. According to beauty tips shared by Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders in their social media tutorials, preparing the skin and securing each layer are key to keeping makeup in place.Primer creates a smoother base for foundation, while setting powder helps reduce excess shine and keeps products from shifting. Setting spray adds another layer of support, making it an important step for anyone who wants makeup to withstand warm weather and a busy day.ONE/SIZE Beauty's primer and setting spray feature among the products repeatedly seen in the cheerleaders' routines. Loose powders also play a major role, particularly around the under-eyes, where makeup can crease or fade. Pink-toned powders from brands such as Rare Beauty and Givenchy are among the options featured in these looks.Application matters just as much as product choice. Rather than relying on one layer of makeup to do all the work, the cheerleaders build their base with care. For everyday wear, however, it is worth adjusting the amount of powder and spray to suit your skin type and comfort level.Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders use layered makeup for lasting resultsOne of the most useful lessons from the cheerleaders' routines is the combination of cream and powder products. They often apply cream-based foundation, contour and liquid blush first, then follow with powder products to help set the colour and add staying power.For example, liquid blush can be topped with powder blush, while a contour stick can be paired with bronzer. Powder may also be applied after cream products and used again to finish the look.This layered method helps create a more durable finish than relying on a single product. Still, applying too much can make makeup look heavy, so blending each layer well is essential.The cheerleaders also keep their touch-up routine simple. Setting powder, blush, bronzer and lipstick are four useful products to carry for quick refreshes. Instead of rebuilding the entire face, you can focus on areas where makeup has faded.For best results, gently remove excess sweat before touching up, then apply only what is needed. articles.title: How Matthew Stafford’s estimated $170 million net worth gives him a $70 million edge over Josh Allen
articles.summary: Matthew Stafford and Josh Allen have built their fortunes in different stages of their NFL careers.
articles.body: Matthew Stafford and Josh Allen have built their fortunes in different stages of their NFL careers. Stafford, the Los Angeles Rams quarterback, has spent years collecting major contracts, including a long run with the Detroit Lions. Allen, meanwhile, has become one of the NFL’s highest-paid quarterbacks after signing a record-setting extension with the Buffalo Bills in 2025. Celebrity Net Worth estimates Stafford’s net worth at $170 million and Allen’s at $100 million. The $70 million difference puts Stafford ahead on paper, though the estimates do not tell the full story of either player’s finances.Matthew Stafford’s estimated $170 million fortuneStafford’s financial lead reflects a career that began in 2009, when the Detroit Lions selected him first overall in the NFL Draft. He spent 12 seasons in Detroit before the Rams acquired him in 2021. That move brought a fresh start on the field and eventually delivered the biggest prize of his career: a Super Bowl LVI title.His earnings have grown through several contracts over the years. Stafford signed a five-year, $135 million extension with Detroit in 2017, then agreed to a four-year, $160 million deal with Los Angeles in 2022. Those contracts helped establish a financial base that Allen, who entered the league a decade later, has had less time to build.Celebrity Net Worth lists Stafford’s net worth at $170 million. That figure is an estimate, not a public accounting of his bank accounts, investments, property, taxes or spending. Still, his years of high-value NFL contracts help explain why his estimated wealth remains substantial even as he enters the later part of his playing career.Josh Allen’s $100 million net worth and massive Bills contractAllen’s path has moved at a different pace. Buffalo selected him seventh overall in 2018, and he developed into the centerpiece of the Bills’ offense. His combination of passing and running ability helped turn him into one of the league’s most recognizable quarterbacks, while his performance has also strengthened his earning power.In March 2025, Allen agreed to a six-year, $330 million extension with Buffalo, including $250 million guaranteed, according to reports on the deal. The contract tied him to the Bills through the 2030 season and put him among the highest-paid players in NFL history by total value. It also gave Buffalo a long-term commitment to the quarterback who has led its push for a Super Bowl appearance.Celebrity Net Worth estimates Allen’s fortune at $100 million, $70 million below Stafford’s reported figure. That does not mean Allen’s contract value is the same as his personal wealth. NFL contracts are paid over time, and headline figures can include guarantees, bonuses and salaries that are subject to taxes, fees and other obligations. Allen’s deal could add substantially to his wealth over the coming years, but its full value should not be confused with money he already has.Why the $70 million gap does not tell the whole storyThe comparison is partly about timing. Stafford entered the NFL in 2009 and has had more seasons to earn and retain money from contracts. Allen arrived in 2018 and secured his biggest deal after establishing himself as a franchise quarterback. A net-worth estimate captures an attempt to measure accumulated wealth, while a contract figure describes potential earnings across a set period.There is also no public, audited balance sheet for either player that confirms the exact totals. Celebrity Net Worth’s numbers offer a point of comparison, not a definitive ranking of their private finances. Endorsements, investments, taxes and personal expenses can all affect the final picture.For now, Stafford holds the estimated edge at $170 million to Allen’s $100 million. Allen’s new contract gives him a major opportunity to narrow that gap, but the comparison today still favors the veteran quarterback. The more revealing question is how much of each player’s future earnings they can turn into lasting wealth once their playing days are over.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “One commitment he wanted to continue”: How Travis Kelce turned his Kansas City charity work into a chance for teens to build skills beyond the NFL
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has spent years making big plays for the Kansas City Chiefs.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has spent years making big plays for the Kansas City Chiefs. Away from the NFL, he has also invested in opportunities for young people in his adopted city. His support for Operation Breakthrough helped students explore robotics, digital electronics and 3D printing through its Smart Lab. The project also helped lay the groundwork for a bigger effort to give teenagers practical skills and more choices as they prepare for life after school.Kelce’s involvement began with a visit to the Kansas City nonprofit in 2015. What he saw there made him look beyond a one-day appearance and consider how he could help children as they grew older.How Travis Kelce’s investment helped expand learning opportunities for Kansas City teensIn an interview with the Los Angeles Times published on Sept. 5, 2024, Kelce recalled his first visit to Operation Breakthrough. He had joined a Kansas City Chiefs community event to read to preschoolers when he noticed how much support the organisation offered families.“I did a community relations deal with the Chiefs and read a Dr. Seuss book to a bunch of preschoolers,” Kelce told the LA Times. He said he looked around and saw that the centre provided meals for children and their families.That visit stayed with him. Kelce later asked Operation Breakthrough president and CEO Mary Esselman what happened to the children once they reached high school. He said the organisation could not accommodate them beyond its existing age range.“And I was like, man, we’ve got to do something about that,” Kelce told in the same interview.His support first included an investment in the Smart Lab. Students could explore robotics, digital electronics and 3D printing, giving them opportunities to work with technology and develop practical skills.Ignition Lab gave Travis Kelce’s youth initiative a bigger purposeKelce’s involvement later grew into the Ignition Lab, a hands-on learning centre created with Operation Breakthrough and MINDDRIVE. He bought a former muffler shop to help expand the nonprofit’s campus and provide a dedicated space for teenagers.The facility offers students practical experience, including automotive work. Its projects allow young people to learn by working with tools and equipment rather than only reading about technical subjects.Esselman also explained why Kelce’s continued involvement mattered to the organisation. In an interview, she said Kelce had told his manager that this was the commitment he wanted to keep because it connected him with the children.“He shared with his manager that this was the one [commitment] he wanted to continue to do because it keeps him connected to the kids,” Esselman told the newspaper.The project reflects a different side of the Chiefs star’s charitable work. His support has helped create space for students to explore interests and build skills they could use in future careers.Kelce’s contribution does not guarantee a particular career outcome for every student. It gives teenagers access to learning experiences they might otherwise miss. articles.title: Josh Allen Called Out by Eli Manning, NFL Fans & Fantasy Managers amid Slow Start vs. Donald, Rams
articles.summary: Josh Allen has had another strong start to the 2026 campaign, but the Los Angeles Rams defense had the Buffalo Bills' quarterback's number in the first half of Monday's game.
articles.body:
Josh Allen has had another strong start to the 2026 campaign, but the Los Angeles Rams defense had the Buffalo Bills' quarterback's number in the first half of Monday's game.

Allen completed just four of his seven pass attempts for 60 yards, adding 21 yards on the ground through the first two quarters. He also had an interception after throwing into double coverage in the final minute of the half.

The Bills still managed to go into halftime leading 13-7 thanks to a few field goals and a touchdown from James Cook III.

Luckily for the Bills and fantasy managers of Allen, he turned things around and finished the night with 210 passing yards, a touchdown and an interception, adding 121 rushing yards and a score on the ground.

Still, he took some heat from Eli Manning of the Manningcast , as well as NFL fans and fantasy managers on social media after the rough start.

Allen was without one of his top targets, DJ Moore, on Monday, which could explain the slow start, but fans were still expecting a bit more from the former MVP in a primetime matchup against one of the NFL's best teams.

His interception late in the first half could be considered what some call an "arm punt" since it was third and long, but it did give Matthew Stafford and the Rams a chance to score since there was still time on the clock. Luckily for the Bills, they didn't capitalize.

Allen came into Monday's game with 1,039 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions, along with 118 rushing yards and seven scores on the ground. He's helped the Bills get off to a 4-1 start, but a rough start on Monday could lead to back-to-back losses for Buffalo.

The Bills typically go as Allen goes, but on nights when he doesn't have it, they'll need a big showing from their defense.

articles.title: "Becoming a mom really put this into perspective for me": Josh Allen’s wife Hailee Steinfeld shares a new baby photo, giving fans a rare glimpse into their family life
articles.summary: Hailee Steinfeld has offered fans another glimpse into her life as a new mother, sharing a photo with her daughter, Harper Haize Allen, in her latest Beau
articles.body: Hailee Steinfeld has offered fans another glimpse into her life as a new mother, sharing a photo with her daughter, Harper Haize Allen, in her latest Beau Society newsletter. The actress also opened up about the small milestones she has been recording as Harper grows. Rather than sharing a conventional baby portrait, Steinfeld chose an image of their shadows together on a walkway. Alongside the photo, she reflected on how motherhood has changed her outlook and why keeping track of her daughter’s development has become a source of comfort.Hailee Steinfeld shares a rare photo with baby HarperHailee Steinfeld included the photo in the latest edition of Beau Society, her newsletter on Substack, published Friday. The image keeps Harper largely out of view, offering a more private glimpse of their time together instead of putting the infant directly in front of the camera.The choice fits the personal nature of Steinfeld’s update. She shared details about watching Harper grow and learning to appreciate moments that might otherwise pass unnoticed."Life is a series of small milestones, and it's worth celebrating them," she stated in the newsletter. "Becoming a mom really put this into perspective for me. Harper is growing into herself so fast."Steinfeld also revealed that she had been writing down Harper’s development milestones in a notebook. She is not sure whether those notes will have a practical use later, but the act of recording them matters to her now."I don't know if I'll ever need the little 6-month update I scribbled in my notebook this week. But having her little growth and development moments down on paper brings me a lot of comfort."That detail gives the update a personal touch. For Steinfeld, documenting Harper’s early months is not simply about keeping a record. It is a way to hold on to changes that can feel rapid when a child is growing up.Hailee Steinfeld reveals her morning ritual with HarperThe newsletter also offered a look at how Steinfeld starts her day with her daughter. She described a simple routine that takes them outdoors together, without the need for an elaborate plan."One of my favorite morning 'rituals' is picking up Harper - both of us still in our PJs - walking barefoot into the backyard and saying 'hi sun,'" she said. articles.title: “When you get to know him, there’s a lot more to him”: Davante Adams’ wife Devanne once revealed the one side of her husband that makes his presence so intimidating
articles.summary: Davante Adams has spent years building a reputation as one of the NFL’s most dangerous wide receivers.
articles.body: Davante Adams has spent years building a reputation as one of the NFL’s most dangerous wide receivers. But his wife, Devanne Adams, has offered a more personal view of the man behind that reputation. In a January 2021 interview with The Ringer, she described her husband as having a “strong, intimidating presence,” before adding that there was much more to him once people got to know him. “When you get to know him, there’s a lot more to him.” Her words gave a glimpse into a personality that fans may not always see on Sundays. The couple, who met at Fresno State University in 2012, have since built a family together and are now parents of four children.What Devanne Adams revealed about her husband’s personalityDevanne’s description of Adams was brief, but it captured the difference between his public image and his private life. On the field, the Los Angeles Rams receiver is known for his sharp routes, reliable hands and ability to make life difficult for opposing defenders. Away from football, his wife has suggested that his personality is more layered than his imposing presence might indicate.Her comments to The Ringer in January 2021 gave readers a perspective that statistics and game footage cannot provide. Devanne did not dismiss the intimidating side of her husband. Instead, she made it clear that it was only one part of who he is.She had offered a similar insight in an August 2018 interview with Bleacher Report, saying that “he doesn’t act like a celebrity. He’s the same old Davante.” The remark came as Adams was establishing himself among the league’s leading receivers with the Green Bay Packers.That distinction matters when considering how long the couple have known each other. They met as college students in California in 2012, before Adams entered the NFL as a second-round pick in 2014. Devanne knew him before professional football brought fame, bigger contracts and constant attention.From college sweethearts to a family of four childrenThe relationship has lasted through several major changes in Adams’ career. After meeting at Fresno State, the couple got engaged in 2017 during a trip to the Bahamas. They married on June 23, 2018, in Pebble Beach, California, and Devanne has remained a familiar presence throughout his NFL journey.Their family grew with the arrival of daughter Daija Leigh in September 2019, followed by Dezi Lynn in April 2022 and son Drayson in August 2024. In April 2026, the couple announced that they were expecting another child. Devanne later shared a video with their newborn at a Rams game, confirming the arrival of their fourth child. They have not publicly disclosed the baby's name, sex or birth date, according to InStyle.Devanne has also celebrated her husband's achievements publicly. In January 2026, she praised his continued success across different teams, writing on Instagram Stories: “Different jerseys, same dominance. Watching my husband be the standard everywhere he goes will never be old.”Her message reflected the pride she takes in Adams' career, even as his NFL journey has taken him from Green Bay to Las Vegas, New York and Los Angeles. Through those moves, their relationship has remained a constant.For Adams, football brings the pressure of performing at the highest level. At home, he has a growing family and a partner who has known him since before his professional career began. articles.title: Former Eagles CB Asante Samuel calls out coach Nick Sirianni after brutal London loss: 'You lost the game'
articles.summary: Asante Samuel ripped Nick Sirianni for skipping a squib kick that let the Jacksonville Jaguars set up a walk-off field goal to stun the Eagles.
articles.body: The Philadelphia Eagles flew all the way across the Atlantic Ocean just to hand a victory to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Unsurprisingly, former All-Pro cornerback Asante Samuel has seen enough. Eight seconds left, a one-point lead, and a squib kick sealed it. Instead, Nick Sirianni gifted Jacksonville a live return, setting up an improbable walk-off win. Speaking on the "Say What Needs To Be Said" show, Samuel put Sunday's 19-17 collapse squarely on Philadelphia's head coach. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "You lost the game for your team," Samuel said. "Of course, the team was going to have his back and say, 'No, coach, it's not on you. It's on us.' But all the coach had to do was call a squib kick. A squib kick at the end of the game is normal and done all the freaking time." Samuel torched Sirianni for his lack of awareness in crunch time. "Nick Sirianni must have had a lapse in his brain or something and wasn't paying attention for him to miss out on that situation," Samuel said. "There's no way your team fights that hard for that long, and you let your team down by not making sure the right call is being made." The blunder erased what should have been a gritty road win. Down Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith to hamstring injuries, Philadelphia took a 17-16 lead with eight seconds left on Jake Elliott's 48-yard field goal. NFL WEEK 5 SUNDAY TAKEAWAYS: RODGERS DEFIES FATHER TIME, COEN GETS BAILED OUT, 49ERS SURVIVE UGLY PERFORMANCE Jacksonville's Ameer Abdullah responded by fielding a clean kickoff, ripping off a 53-yard return, and setting up Cam Little's walk-off 57-yarder as time expired. The loss dropped Philadelphia to 2-3 while pushing the Jags to their third-straight victory. Sirianni fell on his sword Sunday right after the final whistle. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I didn't make the right decision and I lost us that game," Sirianni told reporters. "And that's what I said to our guys. What hurts there is that the guys fought so hard, and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game and I put that fully on me." When asked why Philadelphia left eight seconds on the board before Elliott's kick, Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts made it clear game management was outside his control. "It’s not my place, and we’re prepared, I’m prepared as a quarterback to not worry about those things," Hurts told reporters Monday. "So I’m honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game. When I’m up at night, yeah, I think about, 'Man, should I have said something, or should I have took a step back and said, "Wait"?' But ultimately, there’s a commitment to that and going out there and executing. And so this was one where it did not work in our favor." JALEN HURTS SAVES EAGLES FROM UGLY UPSET AS PHILADELPHIA ESCAPES TITANS TO REMAIN UNBEATEN Sirianni doubled down Monday, shutting down any idea that Hurts should have overruled the sideline. "Jalen’s playing," Sirianni told reporters. "We’re coaching and calling the plays, and Jalen’s got to go execute what we call in that moment, 100 percent. We’re not asking him to make play calls in that scenario. He’s already got enough to worry about to go out and execute. That’s where we were there in that situation." CASE KEENUM'S PERFORMANCE IN WIN OVER EAGLES SHOULD TELL BEARS THIS: DON'T RUSH BACK CALEB WILLIAMS Sirianni can preach staying in your lane all day, but Hurts is losing sleep over brain-dead strategy, and Samuel wants the head coach held to the fire. Good luck fixing that mess. Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

articles.title: Why is Patrick Mahomes being urged to take a stand? Nick Saban and Deion Sanders back controversial college sports bill
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has faced a fresh challenge, but this time it has nothing to do with the Kansas City Chiefs or an NFL opponent.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has faced a fresh challenge, but this time it has nothing to do with the Kansas City Chiefs or an NFL opponent. Sports commentator Dan Le Batard wants the quarterback to speak up about a controversial college sports bill that could limit athletes’ freedom to transfer schools. With Nick Saban and Deion Sanders publicly backing the legislation, Mahomes’ silence has become a talking point in the debate over players’ rights.The Protect College Sports Act of 2026 cleared the Senate on Sept. 28 with a 77-22 vote and now awaits consideration in the House of Representatives. Supporters say it could bring order to college athletics. Critics, however, worry that its restrictions could take away some of the freedom athletes gained through name, image and likeness (NIL) deals and the transfer portal.Dan Le Batard challenges Patrick Mahomes to speak up for college athletesOn his podcast, The Dan Le Batard Show, Le Batard called out Mahomes for staying quiet while prominent football figures support the bill. He also pointed to the quarterback’s influence and his past involvement in discussions about racial justice.“Patrick Mahomes, get your helmet out of your a**. Do some leading here,” Le Batard said on the podcast, urging the Chiefs star to use his platform.Le Batard also referenced Drew Brees, Tom Brady and Jeff Saturday as NFL figures who have taken public positions on important issues. His argument is that Mahomes has enough influence to contribute to a debate affecting the next generation of football players.Mahomes has spoken out before. In June 2020, he joined other NFL stars in a video urging the league to acknowledge its past treatment of players who peacefully protested against racial injustice. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell later admitted the league had been wrong not to listen to its players earlier.That history makes Le Batard’s latest challenge more pointed. He wants Mahomes to use his voice again, this time on college athletes’ rights.Nick Saban and Deion Sanders support the bill despite transfer concernsThe disagreement centres on how much control college athletes should have over their careers. The Protect College Sports Act proposes a national framework for NIL compensation, eligibility and transfers. It also includes an antitrust exemption for college sports governing bodies, raising concerns about how much power the NCAA could regain over athlete movement.Under the proposed transfer rules, athletes would generally face tighter limits on transferring without losing eligibility. Critics argue that restricting player movement without equivalent collective bargaining protections could weaken athletes’ negotiating power.Saban, the former Alabama head coach, has backed the legislation. In a promotional commercial for the bill, he argued that it would protect college sports traditions, student-athletes, women’s sports and Olympic programs.Sanders, the Colorado Buffaloes head coach, has also endorsed it. In his public message supporting the act, he highlighted opportunities for student-athletes and support for historically Black colleges and universities.Their support contrasts with Le Batard’s demand for Mahomes to speak out. The bill has cleared the Senate, but its future depends on the House.As of now, Mahomes has not publicly responded to Le Batard’s criticism in the material cited here, leaving the debate over his potential role in the fight for college athletes’ rights open.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rams’ fumble recovery erased by officials: What really happened in the game-changing decision
articles.summary: The Rams appeared to recover a James Cook fumble in the third quarter of Monday Night Football, but officials quickly took that possession away.
articles.body: The Rams appeared to recover a James Cook fumble in the third quarter of Monday Night Football, but officials quickly took that possession away. An on-field ruling initially gave the ball to Los Angeles, which would have put the Rams near midfield with their lead intact. After a brief discussion, officials reversed the call and awarded possession to Buffalo. No video review was apparent before the change. The Bills kept the ball, drove downfield and scored a touchdown to regain the lead. The unanswered question was simple: what made the officials change their minds?Why officials reversed the Rams’ fumble recoveryCook lost the ball after a Rams defender knocked it out of his grasp. Players from both teams dived into the scramble, and an official initially ruled that Los Angeles had recovered.Then came the reversal.Officials huddled briefly and changed the ruling “after discussion,” giving the ball to Buffalo instead. There was no apparent replay review to clarify the decision, and the footage did not make the recovery obvious.Dion Dawkins came away with the football, but that alone did not settle who had legally recovered it. The replay showed a mass of players fighting for possession, with no clear view of the ball being secured by either team.The original ruling could have made a difference. Had officials kept the call on the field and sent it for review, they would have needed conclusive evidence to overturn it. If the replay had remained unclear, the Rams might have kept possession.Instead, the decision changed before any apparent video review. Fans were left to work out what the officials had seen in the brief conference, and the available footage offered no obvious answer.NFL officials are allowed to confer and correct calls on the field. They do not need a replay review to make every correction. That means the lack of a review does not automatically make the reversal improper. The bigger issue was the lack of a clear explanation for such a consequential change.How the decision helped Buffalo regain the leadThe Rams had held Josh Allen to just four completions in the first half. Recovering Cook's fumble would have given their offense a chance to extend the lead, with the ball near midfield.Instead, Buffalo kept possession and made the Rams pay. The Bills moved downfield and scored a touchdown, putting themselves back in front.That is what made the sequence sting for Los Angeles. The defense had forced the mistake, and the initial ruling appeared to reward that effort. Within moments, the opportunity was gone.The footage did not clearly establish who recovered Cook's fumble, and the officials' quick reversal left an important detail unexplained.
